title: Circuit Lab B 2027
summary: Half to three quarters of the score is a written test on DC circuits and digital logic; the rest is hands-on with breadboards and multimeters. The manual is unusually explicit about what is OUT of scope, and this course stays inside that line.
objectives: Compute current, voltage, resistance, power and energy with correct units in series, parallel and combination DC circuits
Read a schematic, build it on a breadboard, and measure it with an ammeter, voltmeter and ohmmeter
Explain switches, relays, fuses, breakers and GFCIs, and wire a three-way switch
Predict conduction across a PN junction and size a series resistor for an LED
Produce a truth table, a boolean expression and a gate circuit for one another, using De Morgan and universal gates
Work the station tasks: an unknown resistor from voltages, a charger label, a faulty circuit

units.title: Charge, Fields and Static Electricity
units.summary: Where current comes from, and the one law the manual names for charges.
objectives: Apply Coulomb's law qualitatively and by ratio
Name the hazards of static discharge

lessons.title: Charge, Conductors and Insulators
lessons.objective: State the two kinds of charge and the rules of attraction and repulsion, and classify materials as conductors or insulators.

lessons.title: Coulomb's Law
lessons.objective: Use Coulomb's law to compare forces between charges by ratio when charge or separation changes, without a calculator-heavy computation.

lessons.title: The Electric Field
lessons.objective: Describe the electric field around a point charge, read a field line diagram, and give the direction of force on a test charge.

lessons.title: Static: Sources and Hazards
lessons.objective: Explain charging by friction, conduction and induction, and name the hazards of electrostatic discharge and how grounding prevents them.

units.title: Current, Voltage, Resistance and Power
units.summary: Four quantities, their units, and the two equations that connect them. Everything on the written test uses these.
objectives: Give each quantity's unit and symbol
Compute any one of V, I, R, P from two others

lessons.title: Current: Charge per Second
lessons.objective: Define current as charge per unit time, give its unit, and state the conventional current direction against electron flow.

lessons.title: Voltage, Potential Difference and EMF
lessons.objective: Define potential difference and electromotive force, give the unit, and distinguish a source's EMF from its terminal voltage.

lessons.title: Resistance, Resistivity and the Colour Code
lessons.objective: Give the unit of resistance, explain how length, area and material set it, and read a resistor's value from its colour bands.

lessons.title: Ohm's Law
lessons.objective: Apply V = IR to find any one quantity from the other two, and identify from a V-I graph whether a component is ohmic.

lessons.title: Power, Energy and the Kilowatt-hour
lessons.objective: Compute electrical power three ways, and convert between power, time and energy in joules and kilowatt-hours.

lessons.title: DC and AC: Sources, Uses and Hazards
lessons.objective: Contrast direct and alternating current by source, waveform and typical use, and state why the hands-on tasks never use mains AC.

units.title: Series, Parallel and Circuit Analysis
units.summary: Reading a schematic and computing what flows where. Kirchhoff's laws are State and Nationals only.
objectives: Reduce a network to one equivalent resistance
Find the current and voltage at any component

lessons.title: Reading a Circuit Schematic
lessons.objective: Identify the standard symbols for a cell, battery, resistor, lamp, switch, ammeter, voltmeter, diode and LED, and trace a path through a drawing.

lessons.title: Series: One Path
lessons.objective: Compute total resistance, current and the voltage across each component in a series circuit, and say what breaking it anywhere does.

lessons.title: Parallel: More Than One Path
lessons.objective: Compute equivalent resistance and branch currents in a parallel circuit, and explain why total resistance falls below the smallest branch.

lessons.title: Networks That Are Both
lessons.objective: Reduce a mixed series-parallel network to a single equivalent resistance step by step, and build a required equivalent from given resistors.

lessons.title: Open Circuits and Short Circuits
lessons.objective: Predict what happens to current and to each component when a circuit is opened or shorted, and identify both on a schematic.

lessons.title: Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Laws
lessons.objective: State both of Kirchhoff's laws and use them on a two-loop circuit, solving no more than two simultaneous equations. State and Nationals only.

lessons.title: Multimeters, and Where Each Meter Goes
lessons.objective: Connect an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel, use an ohmmeter on an isolated component, and find an unknown resistance from voltage measurements alone.

lessons.title: Breadboards and How the Rows Connect
lessons.objective: Explain a breadboard's internal connections and build a given schematic on one without shorting a rail.

units.title: Switches, Fuses, Breakers and GFCIs
units.summary: The devices that turn a circuit on, off, or off in a hurry.
objectives: Wire a three-way switch with SPDT switches
Say what each protective device senses

lessons.title: Switches: SPST, SPDT and the Three-Way
lessons.objective: Describe SPST and SPDT switches and wire a three-way circuit so either switch toggles the lamp.

lessons.title: Relays: A Switch a Circuit Operates
lessons.objective: Explain how a relay lets a small current control a large one, and identify the coil and contact sides on a schematic.

lessons.title: Fuses and Circuit Breakers
lessons.objective: Explain what a fuse and a breaker each sense and do, and say why a fuse is replaced while a breaker is reset.

lessons.title: Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters
lessons.objective: Explain what a GFCI compares and why it protects a person where an ordinary breaker does not.

lessons.title: Why Current, Not Voltage, Is What Hurts
lessons.objective: State the effect of current magnitude on the body, and name the safety rules the event enforces.

units.title: PN Junctions, Diodes and LEDs
units.summary: One junction only. Everything past a single-junction device is out of scope.
objectives: Predict conduction from a diode's orientation
Wire two LEDs so they are equally bright

lessons.title: Silicon, Doping and Why It Half-Conducts
lessons.objective: Explain what makes silicon a semiconductor and how n-type and p-type doping change it.

lessons.title: The PN Junction
lessons.objective: Describe the depletion region at a PN junction and explain why current passes one way and not the other.

lessons.title: Diodes in a Circuit
lessons.objective: Determine from a diode's orientation whether a circuit conducts, and read the anode and cathode on a symbol and a package.

lessons.title: LEDs and Making Two Equally Bright
lessons.objective: Explain why an LED needs a series resistor, compute that resistor from the supply and forward voltage, and wire two LEDs to equal brightness.

units.title: Logic Gates, Boolean Algebra and Combinational Circuits
units.summary: Truth tables, De Morgan, universal gates and adders. No sequential logic and no clocks.
objectives: Build a circuit that matches a given truth table
Apply De Morgan's law to simplify an expression

lessons.title: Binary, and Adding in It
lessons.objective: Convert whole numbers between binary and decimal and add two binary numbers with carries. No negatives and no fractions.

lessons.title: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR
lessons.objective: Give the symbol and truth table for each of the six gates, and state each gate's output for any input combination.

lessons.title: Building and Reading a Truth Table
lessons.objective: Construct the complete truth table for a two or three input circuit, and design a gate circuit that matches a given table.

lessons.title: Boolean Expressions
lessons.objective: Write a boolean expression for a gate circuit and simplify it using the basic identities.

lessons.title: De Morgan's Law
lessons.objective: Apply De Morgan's laws to convert between AND and OR forms, and use them to rebuild a circuit from a different gate type.

lessons.title: Why NAND Alone Is Enough
lessons.objective: Build NOT, AND and OR from NAND gates only, and state what functional completeness means.

lessons.title: Multiplexers and Adders
lessons.objective: Explain what a multiplexer selects and how a half adder and full adder produce sum and carry.

units.title: The Named Scientists and the Hands-On Tasks
units.summary: Seven people the manual asks for by name, and the station tasks that make up a quarter to a half of the score.
objectives: Attribute each discovery to the right person
Work a station task end to end

lessons.title: Ampere, Coulomb, Kirchhoff, Volta, Ohm, Hertz, Boole
lessons.objective: State what each of the seven named figures contributed, and which unit or law carries their name.

lessons.title: Finding a Mystery Resistor From Voltages Alone
lessons.objective: Determine an unknown resistance in a series circuit using only voltage measurements and a known resistor.

lessons.title: Reading a USB Charger Label
lessons.objective: Read output voltage and current from a charger label, compute the power available, and estimate charging time for a stated battery capacity.

lessons.title: Troubleshooting a Faulty Circuit
lessons.objective: Locate an open, a short or a wrong component in a built circuit using systematic measurement rather than guessing.
